analysis:
The PR changes two documentation files and no executable source. In docs/architecture/inference.md line 1353, the gpt_oss row now says a bf16 checkpoint keeps bf16 activations and native K/V on every layer, citing GPTOSS+Experts.swift `swiglu`. In docs/architecture/prefix-cache.md line 689, the gpt-oss-20b sizing row changes from float32 K/V on 23 of 24 layers to bf16 on all 24 layers. That halves the SSD checkpoint size: 308.0 MB becomes 154.1 MB at 6,144 tokens.

I checked this against T-041, the SSD prefix-cache threat. The documented mitigations are the HMAC lookup tags, AES-GCM/DBK3 encryption, the 30-minute TTL, the disk budget, account-scoped cacheSalt, and the per-donation gate. Nothing in the docs weakens or reverses them. The file-size change affects the accepted residual metadata in T-041, but the size is only a uniform-block-shape property. It does not identify a prefix. The docs do not change TTL, KEK handling, scope derivation, or the kill switch.

The remaining open question is outside the supplied evidence. I could not see the code that backs the claim about bf16 dtype behavior. That includes the dtype/capability gates in the Swift sources and the cache-sizing constants. This is a documentation-accuracy matter that the integration pass may want to confirm. It is not a demonstrated security regression. The other docs text in the supplied excerpts is unchanged context, with no new endpoints, trust boundaries, or attestation claims.
